decision_rationale: The Bay Restaurant has multiple meaningful and actionable Instagram marketing gaps. Reported engagement is substantially below the available food and beverage benchmark, recent posting frequency is relatively low, menu and product visibility are limited, no prices were visible in the analyzed sample, customer-oriented CTAs appeared in less than half of the analyzed posts, and public audience interaction was minimal. The account also has strengths including consistent branding, recognizable positioning, bilingual content, visual variety, and the ability to communicate a delivery product effectively. The qualification is based only on the restaurant's Instagram marketing gaps and supplied evidence; it does not infer revenue impact or business performance outside Instagram.

evidence: The account has 20,474 followers.
Average likes are 6.33 per post.
Average comments are 0.0.
The reported engagement rate is 0.031%.
Analyzed posts received only 1–10 likes each and no comments.
Dash Social’s 2026 Food and Beverage Industry Benchmarks reports an average Instagram engagement rate of 0.4% across the food and beverage industry.
Dash Social also provides a 2.0%–2.5% reference range for strong Instagram performance by food and beverage brands.
The Bay’s reported engagement rate is approximately 13 times below the cited 0.4% industry average.
Reach, impressions, saves, and shares are unavailable, and the restaurant’s engagement-rate methodology is not fully documented.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Improve audience engagement and content performance through stronger, more relevant content and clearer interaction opportunities, while validating performance with more complete reach and engagement data.

evidence: The account published 4 posts in the last 30 days.
The reported frequency is 0.93 posts per week.
The account had gone 10 days without a post at the time of analysis.
Restroworks’ 2025 restaurant social media statistics article references approximately 3–4 quality posts per week as a stronger restaurant posting cadence.
The Bay’s observed frequency is materially lower than that reference.
Posting volume alone does not establish content quality or business results, and the benchmark is directional rather than universal.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Establish a more consistent publishing cadence to maintain visibility for restaurant discovery, food consideration, delivery decisions, and current offers.

evidence: Menu visibility was found in only 1 of 5 successfully analyzed posts.
The menu visibility rate was 20%.
Only one analyzed post clearly presented a detailed product proposition: the Sharing Box.
The Chicken Jalfrezi post showed food but no menu or price.
Two chef-focused posts showed no food or menu.
The kitchen video showed chefs but no food or menu.
No reliable external benchmark was identified for the percentage of restaurant Instagram posts that should include menus or dishes.
Price visibility was 0% across the analyzed sample.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Increase repeated exposure to specific dishes, menu information, and product-selection details within Instagram content.

evidence: Price was visible in 0 of the successfully analyzed posts.
The price visibility rate was 0%.
The Sharing Box post listed multiple food items and delivery platforms but did not show a price or discount amount.
The Chicken Jalfrezi post named the dish but did not show a price.
No analyzed post gave the audience a visible price reference.
No reliable external benchmark was identified establishing a universal percentage of restaurant Instagram posts that should display prices.
The absence of prices in posts does not prove that prices are unavailable through the Linktree or delivery apps.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Provide visible price or offer information where appropriate to help customers assess affordability, compare options, and evaluate promotional products.

evidence: 2 of 5 successfully analyzed posts contained a CTA.
The CTA rate was 40%.
The Sharing Box post directed users to delivery apps.
The wanted-poster carousel asked users to swipe for evidence.
The kitchen, chef appreciation, and Chicken Jalfrezi posts did not include a visible ordering, reservation, visit, or inquiry CTA.
No reliable restaurant-specific benchmark was identified for the percentage of Instagram posts that should contain a CTA.
The majority of analyzed posts lacked a clear customer-action CTA.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Use explicit customer-oriented calls to action more consistently, directing audiences toward ordering, visiting, reserving, inquiring, or using delivery channels.

evidence: Average comments were 0.0.
No comments were recorded on any successfully analyzed post.
Average likes were also very low at 6.33.
The content includes some interactive prompts, but no public discussion was visible in the sample.
No sufficiently comparable restaurant-specific comments-per-post benchmark was identified.
The finding has moderate confidence because private messages, story replies, shares, saves, and other interactions are unavailable.
marketing_gaps.recommendation_focus: Strengthen community engagement and audience interaction through content designed to stimulate conversation, feedback, and participation, while tracking interaction types beyond public comments.

strengths: Clear positioning: the bio identifies the restaurant as refined Indian cuisine in Jeddah.
Consistent branding: the logo and branding were visible in all successfully analyzed posts.
Existing content variety: the account uses images, videos, and a carousel format.
Content themes include food, chefs, kitchen operations, humor, gatherings, and delivery.
Bilingual communication: several captions use both English and Arabic, supporting communication with a broader local audience.
Existing promotional capability: the Sharing Box post identifies the product, its contents, intended group occasion, and delivery availability.
Delivery accessibility: the Sharing Box post displays multiple delivery platforms, including Noon Food, Mrsool, Keeta, ToYou, Ninja, Jahez, and HungerStation.
Some customer-oriented CTAs are present: the Sharing Box post directs users to delivery apps, and the carousel asks viewers to swipe through the content.
Recognizable content personality: chef-focused and humorous posts provide a human and distinctive tone.
Food presentation quality: the Chicken Jalfrezi post provides a visually clear close-up of a prepared dish with descriptive captioning.
data_limitations: Six posts were scraped, but only five were successfully analyzed.
One post failed analysis because of a connection error.
The available sample is small relative to the account’s 432 total posts.
Website clicks and delivery-app clicks are unavailable.
Direct messages and story interactions are unavailable.
The reported engagement rate methodology is not fully documented.
Average likes and engagement figures may be affected by the small and partially analyzed sample.
The benchmark studies use different account samples, definitions, time periods, and methodologies.

Dash Social’s benchmark includes accounts with at least 1,000 followers and includes organic, boosted, and promoted content while excluding paid ads; this may not be directly equivalent to The Bay’s reported metric.
Posting-frequency references are directional benchmarks, not universal performance requirements.
Absence of prices or CTAs in analyzed posts does not prove that the information is unavailable elsewhere, including the Linktree or delivery apps.
Missing data has not been treated as zero except where the supplied research explicitly reported zero, such as average comments and price visibility.
